accuracy.evidence: Uses the everyday comparative vocabulary of early measure correctly: big/small for overall size, tall/short for height standing up, long/short for length lying down. The fair-test steps (line up ends on a start line, take the tower off its box) match the direct-comparison approach in EYFS and Common Core K.MD.A.2 before any units are used.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the classic toddler errors: judging length by which crayon sticks out further when ends are not aligned, thinking a tower on a box is taller, mixing tall with long (a snake is long, not tall) and treating small as the opposite of long. The adult text names these as common mistakes to watch for.

lab_distinct.evidence: A concrete measure lab built only for 2 to 3 year olds: tapping big or small in picture pairs, adding and removing blocks against Bear's 3-block tower, dragging a crayon to a start line, lifting a cat's tower off its box and ordering three bears. It shares no step design with older measurement labs and passed the 30% shingle gate.

lab_teaches.evidence: Steps build the idea in order: size words, then height by building, then length with a shared start line, then why a fair comparison needs the same base, then ordering three objects. The child acts first and the message only confirms what the blocks or crayons already show on the canvas.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong answers: 'The blue crayon sticks out further. Is it the longer one?', 'Bear's tower has 3 blocks. Yours has 1. How do you make yours taller?' and 'Which tower is taller?' with one tower sat on a box. Each is checked on the canvas and the reveal says what the child picked.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions, each wrong option with its own message, for example 'Tall is for things that stand up high. A snake lies down and goes on and on, so it is long' and 'The tower did not change. The chair lifts it up. Count the blocks to check.' No generic try-again text.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short, concrete sentences and passed the family readability gate (kid FK grade at or under 5, adult rewritten from 10.7 to about 7.5). Words like big, small, tall, long and short are always paired with a picture so pre-readers can follow with a parent.

no_filler.evidence: No filler phrases or padding passed the content gate; every sentence either names a size word, gives a comparison rule or tells the parent what mistake to watch for. Explanation duplication is under the 12% limit and the kid explanation stays within four paragraphs.

mobile.evidence: Walked on iPhone 13 and desktop: six steps, five tasks and the challenge all complete, every Show me reaching the tick within 6 seconds. Tap targets are large tiles and buttons sized for small fingers, and dragging the crayon also works by tapping.

accessibility.evidence: axe found no violations in light or dark theme. Every canvas has an aria-label and a live text description of the state (block counts, which crayon is longer), and all choices are real buttons so the lab works without dragging or colour alone.
